title: Build a Count-Min Sketch + Heavy-Hitters Top-K
summary:
Build the probabilistic data structures behind *"design top-K / trending hashtags / heavy hitters"*. You implement a **Count-Min Sketch** (width and depth from ε/δ, seeded MurmurHash3 rows, never underestimates, mergeable across shards), a **top-K heavy-hitters** tracker that pairs the sketch with a size-K min-heap, and **trending in the last N minutes**, which uses time buckets whose sketches are merged at query time.

The judge streams 100,000 Zipf-distributed events. It checks the ε·N error bound, that merged sketches equal a sketch of the whole stream, and that your top-10 matches the exact top-10, all in a fixed amount of memory that does not grow with the number of distinct items.

milestones.name: M1: Hashing and sizing
milestones.description: MurmurHash3 (x86, 32-bit) that matches the reference vectors; `sketchDimensions(ε, δ)` = ⌈e/ε⌉ × ⌈ln 1/δ⌉.

milestones.name: M2: Count-Min Sketch
milestones.description: add / estimate (min over rows) / total; never underestimates; at most a δ fraction of items exceed ε·N on a Zipf stream; more rows mean less error.

milestones.name: M3: Mergeable sketches
milestones.description: Cell-wise merge equals sketching the concatenated stream, which is how per-shard or per-minute sketches combine. Incompatible sketches are rejected; `clone` is independent.

milestones.name: M4: Heavy hitters with a min-heap
milestones.description: A generic `MinHeap`, then `HeavyHitters`: K candidates ranked by sketch count with deterministic tie-breaks. Matches the exact top-10 on 100k events; late risers get in.

milestones.name: M5: Trending in a sliding window
milestones.description: `TrendingTopK` with time buckets: only the last `windowMs` counts, steady items beat one-minute spikes, and memory is bounded by the bucket count.
